_doc: SNG-232 — THE SEAM LEDGER (checkable form). A 'seam' is a place where system A (producer) writes data that
system B (consumer) reads, under an UNSTATED contract both must honor. wiring_audit + content_ci catch WIRING
and SCHEMA; they do NOT catch two individually-valid systems that DISAGREE about the same data (the ~80% bug
class of the 2026-07 session). tests/wiring_audit.mjs §5 (runSeam) gates on the seams declared here.
This file is COMPILED from Aevi's authored ledger (po/staged_content/seam_ledger.json) — her prose contracts
+ checkHints, turned into machine-checkable asserts by CCode (SNG-232 ownership split). Add a future seam by
appending one entry here (grows by incident); author the intent in Aevi's ledger, CCode compiles the check.
DISCIPLINE: DECLARED not inferred (we check listed seams, never auto-discover). GROWS BY INCIDENT. A SEAM
CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS THEATER — every entry reads REAL code (or a REAL covering gate) that a future edit
can break; runSeam self-tests its matcher can go red before trusting any green.
KINDS (Aevi's taxonomy): field_presence (a writer may OMIT a field a reader assumes → reader floors/guards OR
writer fills), field_shape (both ends must agree on TYPE), cross_source (a consumer reads a source a related
producer doesn't feed), enum_vocab (op/id vocab must be the SAME set across contract/handler/prompt).
CHECK MODES (pick by which fields the entry declares):
consumer{file,region?} + assert{requires[],forbids?[]}  — scope to a function (or whole file), regex-assert.
corpus[dir|file...]      + assert                        — scan many files at once (whole-of-engine forbids).
content{dir,requireFields[]}                             — every JSON record in a dir carries the fields
(dotted path = non-null; "name[N]" = array len N).
coveredBy{gate,signature}                                — the seam is gated by ANOTHER mature check; assert
its signature is still present (delete it → red).

seams.contract: A generated location may OMIT dangerLevel; the consumer must floor a missing value (null is NOT 0 — a null-danger place could never roll a fight and starves the pool).

producer.note: a minted location can leave dangerLevel null

seams.canFail: Coerce location.dangerLevel with raw|0 and no null path (null->0): DANGER_FLOOR leaves dangerOf -> red.

seams.contract: Every manifest-listed location MUST carry worldPos{colatitude,longitude} + axisVector[12]. A generated or hand-authored location may omit them; catch it at BUILD (content-time), not late at runtime.

producer.note: location authoring/mint; Aevi's the_old_warden_post once shipped with null worldPos/axisVector

seams.canFail: Ship a location JSON missing worldPos or axisVector[12] -> the record is named -> red (caught at build, not in map/travel at runtime).

seams.contract: The _gen marker's TYPE must agree: the mint writes an OBJECT, but old saves carried _gen:true (boolean); a reader that did property-access threw. The reconcile normalizer heals boolean/missing _gen -> tracking object so no reader crashes.

producer.note: the location mint writes _gen as a tracking object

consumer.note: the gen-tracking-object step heals any non-object _gen before readers see it

seams.canFail: Remove the gen-tracking-object reconcile step: an old boolean-_gen save re-enters unhealed and the first _gen property-write throws again (SNG-216) -> red.

seams.contract: poleIntensity MUST be an object {pole:0..1}, never a float. A content author can write a scalar by mistake; the derived-schema validator catches it.
seams.canFail: Delete the content_ci schema-validation check: a scalar poleIntensity would no longer be caught -> the signature leaves content_ci -> red.

seams.contract: The GM-offer path must read the encounter POOL (eligibleEncountersFor), not ONLY location.encounterSeeds — else SNG-225's pool + SNG-229's bestiary are unreachable through GM offers.

producer.note: eligibleEncountersFor(table, location) = the danger+tag-gated offerable pool

seams.canFail: Revert to a seeds-only offer list: eligibleEncountersFor leaves listAvailableEncounters -> the pool is unreachable again -> red.

seams.contract: A discovery the player can USE must be registered where usability is READ (abilities[] + customAbilities), not only where discoveries are recorded. registerDiscoveryAbility must write the usable ability.

producer.note: registerDiscoveryAbility mints the braid-shaped usable def

seams.canFail: Make registerDiscoveryAbility write only discoveries[] (drop the abilities.push): the intent-parser reads abilities[] and never sees the skill (SNG-226 — earned but uncastable) -> red.

seams.contract: A manifest provides.* key MUST be read by the loader or the content silently doesn't load (provides.bestiary was declared, unread -> creatureIds unresolvable). The rule applies to EVERY new provides.* key.
seams.canFail: Delete the content_ci provides-key/loader check (SNG-065): a declared-but-unread key would no longer fail -> the signature leaves content_ci -> red.

seams.contract: travelTo MUST be a PLACE, never a PERSON. The parser can set it to a person's name; the resolver must cross-check the NPC registry before minting a phantom destination (a pronoun guard alone misses proper-name people).
seams.canFail: Strip the npcRegistry cross-check from personDestination: 'catch Ossian' mints 'Ossian' as a phantom place again (SNG-228) -> red.

seams.contract: Aspirations live at character.practice.aspirations; a top-level character.aspirations read finds nothing and 'proves' absence. No code may read the top-level path.

producer.note: the save nests aspirations under practice

seams.canFail: Add a read of character.aspirations (top-level, not practice.aspirations) anywhere in engine/ or app.js -> the forbidden pattern appears -> red.

seams.contract: Every GM op must exist in the prompt contract, the handler, AND the tracked vocab (SALVAGEABLE_OPS) — a documented op with no handler, or a documented op not salvageable, is a silent dead path.

coveredBy.signature: every documented contract op is salvageable

seams.canFail: Delete the contract<->salvage parity check: a documented-but-unsalvageable op would no longer fail -> the signature leaves wiring_audit -> red. (Runtime emission drift is separately surfaced by See-the-Machine.)

seams.contract: A traditionId the GM emits must resolve against the canonical vocab (CONTENT.traditionIndex); an unresolvable id must be LOGGED as a vocab-miss, never silently dropped (which makes an op look emitted-but-inert).

producer.note: the GM emits markTeacher/standingOps/offerAcquisition with a traditionId; THE PEOPLES block shows the valid ids

seams.canFail: Remove the _opVocabMisses capture: an unresolvable traditionId is dropped silently again (SNG-179 — markTeacher looks emitted, does nothing) -> red.

seams.contract: Every effect TYPE authored on a quest outcome must have a matching case in applyQuestEffects, or the ending silently does NOTHING (falls to default → "unknown"). Aevi's marquee-quest vocab (world_fact/arc/standing/world_arc, and codex_fact by its `fact` field) must each be handled — the prose says the world changes; the effect must make it true.
seams.canFail: Remove a case (e.g. world_fact/standing) from applyQuestEffects: that authored effect drops to default → "unknown" and the ending changes nothing (SNG-235 — the keystone arc's prose promises proof, the world stays empty) -> the pattern vanishes -> red.

seams.contract: A structured quest's `routes` MUST be a {traditionId: string} map and every outcome MUST have a name. A producer handing an ARRAY (or object-valued routes), or a name-less outcome, renders as [object Object] / a blank Resolve button in the quest detail. structuredQuestRecord must normalize both.

producer.note: structuredQuestRecord builds the record from a def of any shape (authored, generated, GM-emitted)

seams.canFail: Revert routes to `def.routes || {}` or drop the outcome-name fallback: an array-routes quest (Erik's Second Thread) renders [object Object] again and the Resolve buttons go blank -> the patterns vanish -> red.

seams.contract: Every npcRegistry entry MUST carry an `id`. findExistingNpc reads `n.id.split(...)` on EVERY npcUpdate, so a single id-less entry throws and aborts the meet — poisoning every SUBSEQUENT person too (no name ever sticks). Writers must stamp id; the reader must guard its absence.

producer.note: the npc_state/ally quest-effect giver stub now stamps `id` (was omitting it, the poison source)

seams.canFail: Remove the id-guard from findExistingNpc: one id-less registry stub throws `n.id.split` and every meet fails again — the CCODE-20 'fourth or fifth name, none sticking' bug returns -> red.

seams.contract: A GM-invented encounter (newEncounter) only REGISTERS a def; a fight STARTS only via a choice carrying its encounterId (onChoice path A). applyTurn must guarantee an engage choice when the GM didn't wire one.

consumer.note: onChoice path A starts an encounter from a choice.encounterId; applyTurn injects the bridging choice

seams.canFail: Remove the engage-choice injection from the newEncounter block: the invented duel registers but nothing engages it -> the CCODE-19 'fight won't start' bug returns -> red.
